brief: GS's weekly US equities color: the week opened with emerging semis demand from long-only buyers but ended in an aggressive, orderly tech sell-off with little defense into the close. Asset managers finished net sellers, reversing early tech demand, while HF flows finished balanced; ETFs hit roughly 31% of tape, the highest level since June. Thursday-Friday, Consumer outperformed on a flight-to-safety rotation out of tech into Staples, aided by beat earnings in restaurants (CMG, WING, EAT) and cruise lines (NCLH, RCL) plus covering in CROX and BOOT. GS flags the S&P 100dma (7614) and CTA medium-term threshold (7554) as levels to watch. Prime data (Oct 29) show L/S gross leverage up to 216.3% and net leverage up 3.6pts to 47%. HFs turned net buyers for the first time in four weeks on short covers; Info Tech led this week's buying but remains heavily net sold in October, and megacap tech was net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions. Fundamental L/S funds are down on the month (Global -3.6%, Asia -9.5%, TMT -12.6% MTD), still positive YTD. Next week: AAPL closes out Q3 earnings, then midterm elections (Kalshi: 65% Dem-sweep odds), jobs data, and QRA tenor details on long-end supply.
